confirmed: Source limitation verified: retrieval.json records no obtained full text, and the complete PolyU repository abstract was read independently. The repository lists embargoed access ending 2028-01-31; no PDF, article body, tables, or appendices were available for verification (https://ira.lib.polyu.edu.hk/handle/10397/118763, Abstract and Open Access Information).

The source.version description is supported: the PolyU record identifies Design Studies, January 2026, volume 102, article 101371 and the four author entries Zhao, X; Zou, J; Siu, KWM; Zhao, T. Crossref, OpenAlex, and Semantic Scholar each returned no abstract, and the Elsevier article API returned metadata with openaccessArticle=false (PolyU record, Source/Authors; Crossref /works/10.1016/j.destud.2025.101371; OpenAlex W7117301876; Semantic Scholar DOI record; Elsevier PII S0142694X25000833).

The abstract explicitly describes a within-subjects study based on the Double Diamond Model, with the same designers completing the traditional and AI-assisted processes. It does not state randomized condition order or any other random assignment, so randomized=not_stated and provisional design_class=other are supported; has_randomized_people_study=false here means no randomized people study was confirmed, not proof of nonrandom assignment (PolyU Abstract, study-design and participant sentences).

Thirty-one designers completed both conditions and 62 design outcomes were evaluated. The 31 people in each arm are the same people, not 62 independent participants; no initial assignment count, attrition count, or rater count is reported. The form correctly retains n_randomized=null and distinguishes people from output counts (PolyU Abstract, participant and output-count sentences).

The agent was developed from behavioral activation clinical guidelines, self-help manuals, and interviews with 20 psychological experts. These experts are not the 31 designers completing both conditions and should not be added to the experimental participant count; the underlying AI model is not identified in the abstract (PolyU Abstract, agent-development sentence).

All three reported outcome quotations exactly match the abstract: AI expert-assisted approaches yield design outcomes with greater effectiveness, completeness, and applicability. The outcomes were evaluated by design and psychology experts, but rating scales, means, standard deviations, test statistics, confidence intervals, and effect estimates are not supplied (PolyU Abstract, output-evaluation and findings sentences).

Core exclusion is supported by 31 completing designers, fewer than the required 50 people, and random assignment remains unclear. Expert evaluation is scored on the produced design outcomes; neither an AI-versus-human-output comparison nor a synthesis is described. context_class=none is reasonable while assignment remains unresolved; a confirmed nonrandom comparison would instead require observational context under the codebook (PolyU complete Abstract; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 3-4).

The one-line finding correctly states 31 designers, 62 expert-rated outputs, and the favorable direction of the three reported outcome differences, subject to the wording correction above. The abstract describes an empirical design study, so the empty synthesis fields do not omit any reported study pool or pooled estimate (PolyU complete Abstract).
summary: The repository abstract confirms 31 designers, 62 expert-rated outputs, and favorable AI-assisted outcome directions; the corrections concern the phrase "no numbers" and two unknown fields that should use "not_stated". Randomized condition order cannot be confirmed, and the 31-person sample is below the core eligibility threshold.
